Probir Neogi, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
SM Maniruzzaman, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2. Muhammad Ali, Advocate—For Respondent No. 4.
parties:
MM Badshah Shirazi ----- Petitioner
Vs
Judge Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. At the instance of the Writ Petitioner, MM Badshah Shirazi, Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate, Dhaka, this Rule was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 2 to 14 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 150 dated 5-2-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996 arising out of the Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 rejecting the application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure-B) shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule are that the Petitioner is the superintendent of Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and he has been directed by the Waqf Administrator, Bangladesh and authorised by the Hossaini Dalan Management Committee to initiate and conduct legal proceedings and to take appropriate steps in respect of the property in question. 

 4. It is stated that historically this case property is an important religion Waqf Estate. The property appertaining to CS plots No. 104 and 105 of CS Khatian No. 11148, Touzi No. 3241-B1, CS Sheet No. 19 of Ward No. 16 under Police Station Kotwali, Dhaka including the land, buildings, tanks, gates, compounds, walls together with many tombs and structures thereon belong to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate, which is a public Waqf having EC No. 11737 (Dhaka). The Hossaini Dalan is an Imambara, which was created and permanently dedicated in the name of God about 350 years ago by Mir Murad, a pious and wealthy Admiral of the Mughal Navy in Bengal, for the public purposes of pious, religious and charitable nature to commemorate the tragic and noble martyrdom of Hazrat Imam Hussain (AS) at Karbala, and has been ever since used, treated and possessed, as such, by the Muslims in general and the members of the Shia community in particular from generation to gene-ration. The Waqf Estate successfully received the patronage and superintendence of the Mughal Emperors, Nawabs and Subedars of Bengal, the East India Company, the Government of India, the Government of Pakistan and finally, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 5. It is also stated that in or about 1844 AD a committee of four Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Alimullah, the founder of the Nawab family of Dhaka, was appointed by the Government of India to superintendent the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. In 1864 another committee of three Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Sir Abdul Gani was appointed to look after the affairs of the Imambara. In 1891 the Government appointed Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After the death of Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah in 1901, his son Nawab Khawaja Sir Salimullah was appointed to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After his death in 1915, his son Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur was entrusted with the same task. He being in sole charge of the Waqf Estate since 1916 was also appointed Mutawalli of the same after the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934 came into force. Subsequently, the said Waqf Estate was registered as a public Waqf in the office of the Waqf Commissioner, East Pakistan under EC No. 11737. Late Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur functioned as Mutawalli of the Estate till he breathed his last on 21-11-1958. Thereafter, the Government of East Pakistan formed a Committee for the management and supervision of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. Justice Ispahani was the Chairman and Nawab Khawaja Hassan Askari and some other leading persons from the Shia Community were the members of the said Committee. After independence of Bangladesh a new Managing Committee was formed with renowned legal expert Mr Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed in the chair. On 30-12-1986 another Managing Committee was formed with Mirza Mehdi Ispahani, in the chair. After his death on 20-1-2004 Mirza Behrooz Ispahani has been appointed the Chairman of the Managing Committee by the Government. Under the guidance and control of the Managing Committee there is a Superintendent to perform his duties of maintenance and management of the Waqf Estate. The petitioner is the present Superintendent of Hossaini Dalan Imambara. 

 6. It is stated that total area of land belonged to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate appertaining to CS Plots No.104 and 105 is 2.8140 acres. Out of the said quantum of land 1. 9300 acres of land appertaining to CS plot No. 105 is under Khas possession of the Waqf Estate which is known as Hossaini Dalan Building Compound. The other part of the Waqf property comprising an area of 0.8840 acre of land is locally known as 'Gas Garden' and appertaining to CS Plot No. 104 and bounded on all sides by pucca walls and on the south by homestead of Md Yakub, on the north by Hossaini Dalan Road, on the east by pucca compound of Hossaini Dalan and on the west by Hossaini Dalan Road and is hereinafter referred to as "the case property." The case property was leased out to one Pearoo Mia Sardar, predecessor in interest of the present respondent Nos. 3 to 14 for a period of fifty (50) years by a registered lease deed dated 21-12-1956 by the then Mutawalli, Nawab Khawaja Habibullah which was executed with the sanction of the then Waqf Commissioner. It was stipulated in the lease deed that after expiry of the lease period in December, 2007 the lessee would hand over vacant possession of the case property to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The lessee had been paying rent to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate through the Mutawalli but subsequently, he became a defaulter in payment of rent. After the death of the original lessee, Pearoo Mia Sardar, his heirs who are the respondent Nos. 3 to 14 took loan from respondent No. 2, the bank and mortgaged the case property to the said bank in collusion with the bank employees concealing the fact that the case property belongs to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The borrowers having defaulted in payment of loan, the bank instituted Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of outstanding loan amount against them. The Suit was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984. But the defendant judgment-debtors having not paid the amount due to the bank in breach of the terms of the compromise, the decree holder bank put the decree on execution by filing the Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991. The petitioner was totally ignorant of these facts till 16-1-1996 on which date he was taken by surprise to see an auction notice in the "Daily Inquilab" wherefrom he came to know that the case property was going to be sold in auction through the said Execution Case. The petitioner immediately brought it to the notice of the Managing Committee of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the Managing Committee asked him to take legal steps in this respect. Accordingly, the petitioner engaged a learned Advocate, gathered information through him from the Court and obtained certified copies and came to know above facts. 

 7. It is stated that the petitioner, thereafter, filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Executing Court stating therein, inter alia, that the property described in schedule No. 1 to the Execution petition is a Waqf property which was leased out to one Pearoo Sardar by a registered lease deed dated 21-12-1956 for 50 years at a yearly rental of Taka 250 only. It has been provided in clause (g) of the lease deed that the lessee will surrender possession of the case property to the lessor on expiry of the lease period. The bank has illegally filed the mortgage Suit without impleading the Administrator of Waqf or the petitioner as a defendant and no notice under Section 81 of the Waqf Ordinance was issued before institution of the Suit nor any notice in the Execution Case given to the Administrator of Waqf in respect of sale of the Waqf property. The defendant judgment-debtors have no right to mortgage the case property to the plaintiff bank, the present respondent No. 2, to secure the loan availed by them. The case property is liable to be excluded from the execution proceeding. The said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996, thereafter, the decree holder Bank (respondent No. 2) and the judgment-debtors proforma opposite parties Nos. 3 to 8 (Respondents Nos. 4 to 9) contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing two separate written objections. The case of the decree holder in its written objection, in short, was that the mortgagors became owners of the case property under the Government after wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest, the petitioner has no right, title and interest in the case land and, as such, the Miscellaneous Case is liable to be rejected. The case of the judgment-debtors in their written objection was identical with that of the decree holder. 

 10. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that having regard to the provisions of Rules 58 to 62 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure and having regard to the consistent documentary and oral evidence produced by the petitioner establishes that the case property belongs to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate therefore, the respondent No. 1 committed an error of law in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case. The learned Advocate further submits that having regard to the registered deed of lease dated 21-12-1956 under the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act (Annexure-C) and particularly, clause 1 (g), the case property being a lease hold property, any charge created or transfer made by the lessee is subject to the terms of the lease and valid up to the period of lease and, as such, the respondent No.1 committed an error of law in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case. 

 11. The learned Advocate further submits that the respondent No. 2 on total misconception of the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and overlooking the special provisions as to the Waqf property in the said Act, has dismissed the Miscellaneous Case wrongly holding that with the wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest, the judgment-debtor lessee became tenants under the Government in respect of the case property, and, as such, the impugned judgment is passed without any lawful authority, as such, it is liable to be declared illegal. 

 16. Further more, the petitioner by filing a Supplementary Affidavit and annex ring therein certain documents in relation to (1) the legal entitlement on behalf of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf estate, for example, documents of restraining the said Waqf estate by the Administrator of Waqfs of Bangladesh and (2) the relevant documents in support of the entitlement in favour of the Waqf. The Supplementary Affidavit further contains documents in relation to disputes regarding Mutation, Records of right, proceedings under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and also sections 30 and 31 of the Bengal tenancy Rule, 1955 settling the ownership thereof, as such, the suit property is a property of Waqf estate on which the Waqf estate has sole entitlement, therefore, the impugned Order passed rejecting an application under Order XXI, rule 58 is not sustainable under the provisions of law which infringed the fundamental right of the petitioner. 

 "(a) In the meantime, the then Government of East Pakistan acquired all rent receiving interests and the late Pearoo Miah Sarder became tenant directly under the Government. SA Khatian No. 2140 of Mouza Lalbagh has been correctly prepared and finally published with plot Nos. 5273, 5274 and 5275 Jote No. 97 with rent. Rent paid regularly to the Government. The petitioner never raised any objection thereof. It is also contended that the RS Khatian No. 1002 has been prepared in the names of heirs of late Pearoo Miah Sarder with respective shares showing therein with a wrong note, and the respondent Nos. 4 to 7 was registered objection and preferred Appeal there from and the concerned authority corrected the said khatian." 

 32. After considering the facts and submissions of the parties and also considering the Writ Petition and annexure therein and the affidavit in oppositions filed by the respondents and annexure therein, it appears that the respondent No. 2 filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of loan amount of money which was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984 in favour of the respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank Ltd. And on breach of the compromise, the Bank put the decree on execution by filing the Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 and on 16-1-96 an auction notice was published for selling the mortgaged property. It is admitted by both the parties that the said property was originally belonged to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the respondent No.4 to 7 are the heirs of Pearoo Miah Sarder who obtained a lease from the Waqf Estate by a Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 executed by Nawab Khwaza Habibullah Bahadur as a Mutualli of the Dhaka Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate as a lessor. The said deed contains several terms and conditions to be fulfilled and satisfied by the lessor and by the lessee. The said Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 contains the following important terms: "11) The lessor hereby agrees with the lessee as follows:— 

 Nothing in this clause shall be deemed to authorize a tenant having an untransferable right of occupancy, the farmer of an estate in respect of which default has been made in paying revenue, or the lessee of an estate under the management of the Court of Wards, to assign his interest as such tenant, farmer or lessee:" 

 41. In relation to an alternative remedy provided by the statutory provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, it is true that there is an efficacious remedy available for the petitioner to challenge the impugned Order passed by the executing Court on an application under order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure as it is appealable. However, in our jurisdiction there are a number of cases wherein this Court and the Hon'ble Appellate Division decided that where an illegality or error of law is apparent on the face of record of the Sub-ordinate Courts an alternative remedy is not a bar to invoke the writ jurisdiction under article 102 of the Constitution. Applying the aforesaid provisions settled by both in the English Jurisdiction and of our jurisdiction, in the instant case we find it clearly from the records and from the respective submissions made by both the parties that the clear factual position is that the suit property admittedly belong to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate which was registered with the Waqf commissioner under the Waqf Act 1934 and thereafter the same has been registered with the Waqf Administrator of Bangladesh by the number of EC 11737 under the provisions of Waqf Ordinance of 1962. Thereafter, whoever came as the successors claiming their entitlement on the Waqf Property or mortgagee Bank lending money on misreading the vital terms and conditions of the Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 shall be subject to return the property under the liabilities attached to the lease which is also subject to the provisions under the Transfer of Property Act and the Waqf Ordinance 1962. 

 42. From the aforesaid conditions of the lease and pursuant to section 108 (B)(j) of the Transfer of the Property Act, it is obvious that the lessor is entitled to get back the property after expiry of 50 years tenure of the lease period. In the event of the property be transferred or mortgaged or retransferred during the tenure of the lease deed, the transferee or the mortgagee or anybody can only get interest given for or during the valid period of lease, and such interest is subject to any liability attached to the lease deed. In view of the above, the Artha Rin Adalat and subsequently the Artha executing Adalat can only pass an order against the lessee the Judgment-debtor or successors thereof as their personal liability because the mortgaged property is subject to encumbrance of the lease deed dated 21-12-1956. Moreover, the decree holder bank shall become part of the terms and conditions of the Lease Deed. Accordingly, after expiry of the lease period of the lease deed, the present petitioner as a Mutawalli of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate is entitled to get the suit property back at its present position without any liability for the loan granted in favour of successors of the lessee Judgment-debtors, however, the decree holder Bank certainly has remedies for realization of the decretal amount as per provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 44. During the hearing of the Rule the learned Advocates for the respondents submit that in the impugned Judgment there is a contention that the predecessor of the present respondent Nos. 3 to 7 got an interest from the Government under the provisions of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 known as "Rent Receiving interests held under Waqf. It is also submitted that such interest was obliged under Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. 

 47. Besides the above, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.4 informed us that he does not have any document to show as to the acquisition of land by the lessee from the Government, therefore, we are not deciding as to the legality of the loan granted by the respondent bank but we are here to decide whether the respondent Nos. 3-7 were entitled to mortgage the property beyond the tenure of the lease period and whether the Bank can sell the property after the expiry of the lease period or not in default to repay the loan amount. Our view is that the borrower borrowed and the lender leaned the money with full knowledge as to the terms and conditions of the lease deed, therefore, the matter of loan is simply a matter between the present respondent Nos.4 to 7 as successors of the lessee who are the judgment-debtors and the decree holder Bank but the petitioner as the lesser cannot be held liable for loan after expiry of the lease period.
